summary: Added the pure §6 encounter rules as @pirate-sea-race/simulation/encounters (geometry.ts: supercover LOS, bearing by max dot product, circular cones, squared ranges; modes.ts: full sea rules + foot placeholder; state.ts: config/state/events/markers; step.ts: stepEncounters/replayEncounters) and the tuning as @pirate-sea-race/content/encounters (constants in seconds converted to ticks, zod validator). One subpath export added to each of packages/simulation/package.json and packages/content/package.json (source condition first); no postbuild, dependency, barrel or tsconfig changed. Tests: content validator test (negative duration, range above sight radius), geometry tests (supercover equals an exact rational reference on all 6561 pairs of a 9x9 grid, both directions; land blocks, shoals do not; ±4/±8 cone boundaries; exact squared-range boundary), 43 scripted rule tests, and seeded property tests over the slice sea and three synthetic maps (40 seeds x 1600 ticks: invariants every tick, replay hash equality, EXERCISED coverage of every event kind and reason, input reorder and two order-preserving relabellings). docs/encounters.md written. Executed locally after npm ci: npm run typecheck (exit 0), npm run test:unit (684 passed), npm run test:integration (37 passed), npm run build (exit 0, smoke passed); also imported both new subpaths from dist/ by hand.
open_assumptions: A defender who becomes ineligible during the windup (e.g. reserved by someone else's hit on an earlier tick) makes the attempt a miss with cooldown, following §6/the task literally; only same-tick losses are preemptions.
An attacker who disconnects, leaves the snapshot, changes mode or is reserved during the windup has the attempt cancelled (no cooldown).
End reports are also accepted while a duel is still in transition (quit or server fault before the fight starts).
Protection and respawn durations count from the ticks named in the reports (settlement tick, fight end tick), not from the tick the report arrives.
Duel markers carry only {x, y, startTick} with startTick = reservation tick; no duel id because the id contains player ids.
The encounter position is the floor midpoint of the two players at the hit; respawn opponents are every other snapshot player not respawning (disconnected and dueling players included).
If no pair of draw points exists within 6 tiles, both ships stay where they were (documented fallback).
